result.title: OGDA: Ontology-Grounded Data Agents for Reliable Analysis over Heterogeneous Data Lakes
result.summary: Full-pipeline data analysis over real-world data lakes requires LLM agents to locate and integrate information across large collections of tables with different schemas. Existing data agents follow task-specific exploration, which exhausts the context window in massive lakes. As the context fills, the agent's reasoning degrades, leading it to locate and process incorrect data files. These errors propagate into the final answer. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Ontology-Grounded Data Agent (OGDA), which utilizes a compact ontology to reduce exploration overhead and constrain data processing. OGDA constructs the ontology through agentic hypothesis testing. At each step, a proposer agent induces schemas, concepts, and relations from raw sources, and a verifier checks each proposal against the underlying data. During task execution, the ontology serves as a representation of the data lake for the agent to explore. Every data-processing action is constrained by a task graph, which the agent can extend only after observing the semantic meaning of the data. Across KramaBench and DiscoveryBench with three LLM backbones, OGDA outperforms the strongest baselines by up to 10.82 points. These results suggest that explicitly modeling the data lake is a key step toward reliable end-to-end data agents.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 OGDA，用紧凑本体刻画异构数据湖，由 proposer 从原始数据源归纳 schema、概念与关系、verifier 对照底层数据校验，执行时以本体作为数据湖的表示并用任务图约束每一步数据处理动作，在 KramaBench 与 DiscoveryBench 上超过基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「紧凑抽象表示 + 校验器核查 + 动作受图约束」的线索，可能与 LVR 中压缩任务相关状态、筛选视觉证据及限制状态扩展的可核查机制有关。
